title: The Steady Pipeline Setup Checklist: Book Sales Calls Every Week
description: The setup checklist from the reel: the list, domains, inboxes and a weekly sending rhythm so booked calls land every week, not in bursts.
lead: This is the full setup checklist from the reel. An empty day never comes back, so the goal is a steady flow of sales calls every week, not a panic week of outreach. Here's how to set up the list, the inboxes and the weekly rhythm that keeps calls coming.
insider: We run client campaigns as a steady weekly flow, not in bursts. One agency client got **about 100 interested replies a week, every week, for four and a half months**, 2,146 in total. The checklist is the easy part. Building the list, keeping dozens of inboxes healthy and answering every reply is the work we do for clients.

blocks.text: Many owners notice around day ten that nothing is booked. Then they do a panic week of outreach, get busy with the new work, and stop. The next month starts empty again. That's a burst pattern, and it always leaves empty days.

Bursts also hurt deliverability. [Google's sender guidelines](https://support.google.com/mail/answer/81126) warn against sudden volume spikes and say you can increase volume faster when you send **daily instead of weekly**. Steady sending is safer, and it keeps calls coming.

head: Burst outreach
Steady system
rows: Full one week, empty the next

items: Pick one buyer: industry, company size and job title.
Build enough leads for a full month, not just a week. (See the math below.)
Verify every address. Instantly says keep bounces **under 2%**.
Split the list into small groups of one buyer type. [Hunter's 2026 report](https://hunter.io/the-state-of-cold-email) found sequences with 21–50 recipients got **6.2% replies vs 2.4%** for 500+.
Send from separate lookalike domains, never your main domain.
Set SPF, DKIM and DMARC on every sending domain. Our [DNS records guide](/blog/dns-records-for-cold-email.html) has the values.
Max 3 inboxes per domain, about 30 cold emails per inbox per day at full volume.
Warm up for 14 days, then ramp slowly. [Instantly's 2026 report](https://instantly.ai/cold-email-benchmark-report-2026) recommends building up over 4 to 6 weeks.
Keep 1 spare domain warming so a tired inbox never stops the flow.

blocks.text: **Why:** a steady flow needs new people entering the sequence every week, and follow-ups going out on schedule. Instantly found **42% of replies come from follow-ups** and recommends 4 to 7 touches, 3 to 4 days apart, in a Mon → Wed → Fri rhythm.

head: Day
What happens
rows: New leads start email 1. Answer weekend replies first thing
Follow-up 1 goes to Monday's leads. Check bounces
Follow-up 2 goes out. Add next week's leads to the queue
Answer every reply within a few hours and offer two meeting times

blocks.text: Worked example: how many emails for a steady month
Say you send **100 cold emails a day** for 30 days and hit Instantly's average reply rate of **3.43%**.

items: 100 × 30 = **3,000 emails** a month.
In our full-quarter case study, about 1 in 4 replies came from a buyer who wanted to talk (1,061 of 4,372). 103 × 24% = **about 25 interested buyers** a month.
That's about **6 interested buyers a week**, every week, instead of a burst and a gap.
Inboxes needed: 100 ÷ 30 = 3.3, round up to **4 inboxes** on **2 domains**, plus 1 spare domain.

blocks.label: Use your own numbers
blocks.text: Your reply rate and interest rate will differ. Track them for 4 weeks, then redo this math with your real numbers.

items: Reply fast. A buyer who wrote back today may forget you by next week.
Offer two specific times, plus a booking link.
Send a short reminder the day before the call.
Track every interested reply until it's booked or closed out.

blocks.label: AI prompt: plan your steady month
blocks.text:
I want [number] sales calls a month. My offer is [your offer] and my buyer is [job title, industry, company size].

Assume a 3.43% reply rate and that 1 in 4 replies is interested. Tell me:
1. How many emails I need to send per month and per day.
2. How many leads I need for the month.
3. How many inboxes (30 emails per inbox per day) and domains (3 inboxes per domain) I need, plus 1 spare.
4. A simple weekly schedule for sending and follow-ups.

faq.a: Referrals are great, but you can't control when they come. A steady outbound system adds calls you can plan around.

faq.q: How long until calls come in every week?
faq.a: Plan for about 5 weeks to full volume: 2 weeks of warm-up, then a ramp. Replies start once sending starts.

faq.q: How many emails do I need?
faq.a: Work backward from your goal. At a 3.43% reply rate, 3,000 emails a month is about 103 replies. Track your own numbers and adjust.
